signatures.name: CSWH WebSocket Port Scanning
signatures.description: Detects WebSocket connections (ws:// and wss://) to RFC-1918 private ranges and loopback addresses. Covers IPv6 loopback (::1). Octet ranges capped at {1,3} to reduce backtracking. wss:// coverage is essential — CSWH pivots through internal services over encrypted TLS tunnels as readily as plaintext.

signatures.name: Credential Exfiltration via Network Tool
signatures.description: Detects a network tool co-occurring with a known credential variable name, a live AWS access key (AKIA prefix + 16 Base32 chars), an OpenAI/Anthropic sk- token (>=20 chars to avoid short IDs), or a JWT bearer token (three Base64url segments). Note: watcher.py sanitize_log_line() strips '$' before this signature runs, so patterns match bare variable names (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID not $AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID).

signatures.name: Base64 Exfiltration Pipeline
signatures.description: Detects base64 encoding in proximity to a network transmission tool. Note: watcher.py sanitize_log_line() strips '|' before this signature runs, so 'cat /etc/passwd | base64 | curl' arrives as 'cat /etc/passwd  base64  curl'. Proximity matching (within 200 chars, bidirectional) catches this correctly without requiring a literal pipe character.

signatures.name: System Prompt Override / Jailbreak
signatures.description: Detects indirect prompt injection and jailbreak attempts embedded in agent input. Covers: (1) ignore-previous-instructions variants including system/prior/above/earlier/initial; (2) persona reassignment (you are now / act as / pretend to be); (3) DAN, developer, sudo, god, unrestricted mode keywords; (4) override-safety and forget-training; (5) simulate-no-restrictions family. False-positive guards: 'act as both X and Y', 'summarize previous instructions', and 'acts as coordinator' all pass cleanly.

signatures.name: Reverse Shell Indicators
signatures.description: Detects reverse shell establishment. Note: watcher.py strips '>' so 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/' arrives as 'bash -i   /dev/tcp/'. Detection anchors on /dev/tcp/ and /dev/udp/ which survive sanitization intact. Hostname support: [^\s/]+ catches domain names in addition to IP addresses. nc combined flags: -[a-zA-Z]*e[a-zA-Z]* catches -e, -ev, -elp etc. Covers: socat TCP exec, mkfifo /tmp/ staging, Python/Perl/Ruby/PHP one-liners. Safe negatives confirmed: /dev/null, nc -lvp (listen only), mkfifo /var/run/.

signatures.name: Cloud Metadata Service Probe
signatures.description: Detects agent-initiated requests to cloud instance metadata services: AWS IMDSv1 and IMDSv2 (169.254.169.254), AWS IPv6 IMDS (fd00:ec2::254), GCP metadata server (metadata.google.internal), Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254 shared), Oracle Cloud IMDS (169.254.169.254 shared), Amazon DNS (169.254.170.2). These endpoints serve live IAM credentials, user-data scripts, and instance identity documents. There is no legitimate reason for a monitored agent to query these endpoints directly. Applied at pre_tool scope: tool_args are not sanitized, so raw URLs are matched.

signatures.name: Persistence Mechanism Injection
signatures.description: Detects persistence establishment attempts — the second stage of most agent compromise scenarios after initial access. Covers: (1) SSH authorized_keys writes (path presence sufficient — >> is stripped by sanitizer); (2) Cron injection via /etc/crontab, /etc/cron.d/, or crontab -e; (3) systemd service installation via systemctl enable or /etc/systemd/system/ path; (4) User creation/modification: useradd (any arguments), usermod with account-altering flags (-a/-G/-s/-u), chsh shell change; (5) Critical file modification: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, /etc/hosts.allow, /etc/rc.local. Sanitizer note: >> redirection markers are stripped, so detection anchors on the destination path or command name, not the write operator.
